patch.vs_round_1: router.py: _local_mask returns mask[start:start + local_rows] before any cache work when the rank has no pad rows (start + local_rows <= num_tokens <= mask.shape[0]); the tail-rank cache path is round 1's, with the layout values read once. Tests: one assertion of round 1's inference-mode test changed (every rank keeps masks -> only the tail rank does), one new test (8 cases).

change: On a rank whose local slice has no pad rows (every rank when TP divides T, all but the last otherwise), _local_mask now returns the view mask[start:start + local_rows] directly: the same view sp_rows.local_slice(mask[:num_tokens]) returns (same base, data pointer, shape and strides), made with one tensor slice instead of 1107's two, with no key built and nothing read from or kept on the ForwardContext. A mask shorter than T falls through to local_slice, which refuses it as in 1107. The tail rank (pad rows present) keeps round 1's per-forward cache of its new padded tensor, and the pad=True fix in _partials_mask is unchanged.
why_not_stale: Ranks without pad rows keep nothing: each call makes its view from the mask it is handed, as 1107 does, so there is no entry that could be stale. A view also shares the mask's storage, so it can never disagree with the mask.

Tail rank, unchanged from round 1: entries live on the forward's own ForwardContext, and the runner creates a new one for every forward, so no entry outlives its forward although the runner's persistent buffers keep their storage across steps.

Tail rank: the entry holds the mask tensor and a hit requires entry[0] is mask, so the id in the key cannot be reused by another tensor while the entry lives. No version counter is read (inference tensors have none).

Tail rank: a forward's is_padding and input_ids are filled before it runs and not written during it, and routed/image are new tensors each forward that nothing writes after their kernel; 1107 already relies on this for the routed and image masks it keeps on the context by identity.
Tail rank: num_tokens, world_size, rank, rows and pad are in the key, so another layout in the same forward gets its own entry.

Tested: test_gate_router_route_local_masks_last_one_forward (persistent buffers refilled in place across three forwards, each routed with its own masks) passes on both boots; exact_996 shows 0 entries per step on ranks without pad rows and 2 on the tail rank.

premise_check.what: Round 1 attributed the non-tail slowdown to the cache lookup on ranks whose slice is already a cheap view. Measured host cost on sp8 (cpu_996.py: one later routing layer's mask calls, 2000 calls x 7 repeats, three _local_mask bodies interleaved in one process, two boots; slice_cost.py):
premise_check.one_view_vs_lookup_ns: a tensor slice costs 665-735 ns, two slices (1107) 1304-1523 ns, the 6-tuple dict hit round 1 uses 102 ns
premise_check.conclusion: The premise does not hold: round 1's lookup was already cheaper than 1107's view, by about 3-4.5 us per layer of host work, and the GPU work on ranks without pad rows is identical in 1107, round 1 and round 2 (no kernel is launched for a view). This host work runs after the gate GEMM (or partials GEMM) launch, so it overlaps GPU work and cannot slow a GPU-bound call. Skipping the cache for views costs about 1-1.8 us per layer of host work against round 1, still 1.9-2.9 us less than 1107.

parts.part: round 1's tests, its 6 new ones included

reason: Round 2 skips the cache for ranks whose slice is a view, as asked, and keeps everything else round 1 achieved: the tail gain (now 5 of 5 cells beyond the interval), bit-exactness under inference mode, the stale-mask guarantees and the tests (one round 1 assertion about views being kept is changed). It still misses the literal mark: 2 non-tail per-call cells (TP3 T4096 rank0 by 0.03 us, TP4 T16384 rank0 by 3.0 us, 0.9%) and 3 pass cells are slower than the recorded 1107 boots beyond their two-boot interval. The data does not attribute these to the patch. The premise of the fix is false: round 1's lookup was cheaper than the view it replaced, the non-tail GPU work is identical, and the in-process A/B finds all three cells within. Unchanged round 1 code re-run in this session lands slower in a different set of cells. Against a reference interval recorded in another session, no change confined to the mask path can make these GPU-bound cells reliably not slower; whether to accept that is the owner's call.
caveats: The verdict applies the mark literally to both timings of the own-mark bench against the recorded 1107 boots, which are not re-measured.

The round 1 control's first cell (TP3 T768 rank0) was 133 us per call on both control boots against 37-39 us everywhere else, a disturbance on the shared host that was not explained; round 2's boots did not show it. It does not enter the verdict.
Other agents shared sp8 during the batch; every GPU command ran under the GPU lock, and docker_ps lines are recorded per run. bench-r2-boot1's start_utc includes a wait on the lock.

The harness uses a stand-in ForwardContext and plain scratch, as the PR's tests do; it does not run the SP gather collective or a cluster boot. A tp3-switched boot of the corrected stack is still to be done in a candidate window.
